plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of slender silver-green stems topped with fragrant violet-blue spikes hum with bees and perfume the warm air. In Provence, the fields reach their peak display in mid-to-late June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in Provence, with the first blooms opening in mid-June
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Big, rounded clusters of tiny flowers crowd together into puffs the size of a grapefruit. They brighten shady gardens and cottage fences with shades from sky blue to rosy pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Gardens in the eastern United States, the United Kingdom and Japan
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry changes the color. Acidic soil lets the plant take up aluminum, which turns the blooms blue, while alkaline soil produces pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Glossy round pads float on still ponds, and from them rise star-shaped white flowers with golden centers. The blooms open in the morning sunshine and close again by afternoon.
plants.location: Lakes and slow-moving ponds across Europe, from the British Isles to Scandinavia
plants.funFact: The flower stalks are long and flexible. They can reach down several meters to anchor the plant in the muddy bottom.
